;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2020 Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**[[Republic of Artsakh|Artsakh]] [[Ministry of Defence (Artsakh)|Defence Minister]] [[Jalal Harutyunyan]] is seriously wounded in an [[Azerbaijan]]i [[drone strike]] on his vehicle in [[Nagorno-Karabakh]]. He is replaced by Mikael Arzumanyan until he recovers from his injuries. [https://en.armradio.am/2020/10/27/jalal-harutyunyan-wounded-mikael-arzumanyan-appointed-artsakh-defense-minister/ (Public Radio of Armenia)]
**Azerbaijan says an [[Armed Forces of Armenia|Armenian]] missile attack on the city of [[Barda, Azerbaijan|Barda]] killed at least four civilians and injured 13 others. [https://caspiannews.com/news-detail/armenian-cluster-missile-kills-4-azerbaijani-civilians-injuring-13-in-barda-city-2020-10-27-32/ (Caspian News)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[2020 Peshawar school bombing]]
***Eight students are killed in a bombing at a [[madrasa]] in [[Peshawar]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-54701753 (BBC News)]
*An [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] inmate kills a guard and wounds three others with a metal object at a prison in [[Rabat]], [[Morocco]]. The fate of the militant, who was arrested a month ago, is unknown. It is the first terrorist attack in the country since the 2018 [[Murders of Louisa Vesterager Jespersen and Maren Ueland|murders of two Scandinavian tourists]]. [https://www.thedefensepost.com/2020/10/28/morocco-prison-guard-killed/ (The Defense Post)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Zeta]] makes landfall on the [[Yucatán Peninsula]] as a [[Category 1 hurricane]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/hurricane-zeta-new-orleans-louisiana-tropical-storm-warning-mexico-storm-surge-forecast-weather (Fox News)]
**[[Tropical cyclone warnings and watches|Hurricane warnings]] are issued by the [[National Hurricane Center]] across the [[Gulf Coast of the United States]] from [[Morgan City, Louisiana]], to the [[Mississippi]]–[[Alabama]] border. [https://www.foxnews.com/us/hurricane-zeta-new-orleans-louisiana-tropical-storm-warning-mexico-storm-surge-forecast-weather (Fox News)]
*The [[Greek Navy]]'s mine countermeasures vessel {{ship|HS|Kallisto}} is cut in two in a collision with a [[container ship]]. [https://www.newgreektv.com/news-in-english-for-greeks/greece/item/33042-huge-merchant-ship-cuts-minesweeper-kallisto-in-two (New Greek TV)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
******[[Mayor of New York City|New York City Mayor]] [[Bill de Blasio]] asks residents to avoid traveling out of state during the upcoming holidays. For those who decide to travel, he urges them to get tested and quarantine for two weeks. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/10/27/new-york-city-mayor-asks-residents-to-avoid-traveling-out-of-state-during-the-holidays.html (CNBC)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arkansas]]
*****[[Arkansas]] surpasses 100,000 COVID-19 cases and sets a new record of 27 new hospitalizations, bringing the total to 676. [https://katv.com/news/local/arkansas-gov-asa-hutchinson-to-give-covid-19-briefing-10-27-2020 (KATV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kentucky]]
*****[[Governor of Kentucky|Governor]] [[Andy Beshear]] reports a record-high number of new infections in the state with 1,786 cases. [https://www.courier-journal.com/story/news/2020/10/27/kentucky-coronavirus-state-sets-another-record-covid-19-cases/3749167001/ (''Courier Journal'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
*****[[Wisconsin]] reports 5,262 new cases and 64 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, setting a record number for both new cases and deaths since the pandemic began, according to data from the [[Wisconsin Department of Health Services]]. [https://wkow.com/2020/10/27/covid-cases-tuesday-record/ (WKOW-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba]]
*****[[Manitoba]] reports 184 new cases, its highest number since the pandemic began. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/manitoba-covid-19-update-tuesday-oct-26-1.5778519 (CBC)]
****[[Canada]] surpasses 10,000 [[COVID-19]] deaths. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/health/coronavirus/few-outlets-for-grief-as-covid-19-death-toll-surpasses-10-000-in-canada-1.5163312 (CTV)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mayor of Mexico City|Mexico City Mayor]] [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] tests positive for COVID-19 but is asymptomatic. [https://mexiconewsdaily.com/news/coronavirus/mexico-city-mayor-tests-positive-for-coronavirus/ (''Mexico Daily News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]]'s [[Federal Service for the Oversight of Consumer Protection and Welfare|Rospotrebnadzor]] orders all people to wear masks in crowded places starting tomorrow and recommends all restaurants and other late-night establishments to close between 11:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. local time, with all public events banned during that time. [https://www.barrons.com/news/russia-tightens-virus-restrictions-as-cases-spike-01603788904?refsec=afp-news (''Barron's'')]
****Russia reports a record of 320 new deaths in the past 24 hours, taking the nationwide death toll since the [[pandemic]] began to 26,589. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2020/10/27/recorddeaths-a71863 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bulgaria]]
****[[Bulgaria]] reports 2,243 new infections, a new record of cases since the pandemic began. [https://www.novinite.com/articles/206309/COVID-19+in+Bulgaria%3A+Black+Record+of+2243+Daily+Cases+and+42+Deaths (Novinite)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] reports 523 new fatalities in the last 24 hours, which includes 292 people that died in hospitals and another 231 people who died in nursing homes. This is the highest number of daily fatalities since the first wave in April, as [[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] prepares to announce new restrictions tomorrow. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/france-sees-523-covid-19-deaths-highest-in-6-months/2021436 (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports 1,259 new infections, the highest number in a single day, bringing the nationwide total to 32,752. [https://neoskosmos.com/en/178507/greece-records-1259-covid-19-cases-in-unprecedented-negative-record/ (Neos Kosmos)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The number of new confirmed cases in [[Italy]] rises by a record 21,994 in the past 24 hours. In addition, the country also reports 221 new fatalities, the highest daily death toll the country has had since May. [https://www.ansa.it/english/news/general_news/2020/10/27/covid-record-infections-almost-22000-221-victims_88e01880-0d46-43a9-9956-959792318e32.html (ANSA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[La Rioja]] orders the closure of restaurants and bars in its two largest towns, [[Logroño]] and [[Arnedo]], for a month in an attempt to curb the second wave of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-spain-la-rioja/spains-wine-region-la-rioja-shuts-restaurants-bars-for-a-month-idINL8N2HI4EG (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] announces that it will reopen public beaches and increase the number of people allowed to sit together in bars to four people, and at restaurants to six people, on October 30, as part of a relaxation of [[social distancing]] measures. The [[Government of Hong Kong|city's government]] also said that those venues will be allowed to run on-site services until 2:00 a.m. local time. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/hong-kong-economy/article/3107221/hong-kong-beaches-reopen-friday-more-people (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports 6,968 new cases and 346 deaths in the past 24 hours, its highest daily tally since the pandemic began, pushing the death toll to 33,299 and cumulative total cases to 581,824. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1754856/middle-east (Arab News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]]
***[[President of Algeria|President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] is hospitalized at a military hospital in [[Algiers]], days after he went into self-isolation after suspected COVID-19 cases amongst his aides. [https://news.yahoo.com/algeria-president-hospitalised-amid-covid-180730010.html (AFP Via Yahoo! News)]
**The [[United Nations]] cancels all in-person meetings at its [[Headquarters of the United Nations|New York City headquarters]] after five people on the [[Niger]] mission tested positive. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-un/u-n-in-new-york-cancels-in-person-meetings-due-to-covid-19-infections-idUSKBN27C2C6?il=0 (Reuters)]

;International relations
*Aftermath of the [[murder of Samuel Paty]]
**Thousands rally in [[Bangladesh]]'s capital [[Dhaka]] calling for a [[boycott]] of [[France|French]] goods over [[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]]'s defense of cartoons depicting the [[Islamic prophet]] [[Muhammad]], which Muslims consider to be [[Islam and blasphemy|highly blasphemous]]. Police prevented the protesters from reaching the French Embassy. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/27/thousands-rally-in-bangladesh-calling-for-boycott-of-french-goods (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Iran]] summons the French [[ambassador]] over Macron's "insulting comments" regarding Islam and Muslims. [https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/rest-of-the-world-news/iran-summons-french-envoy-over-prophet-muhammads-alleged-insult-by-macron.html (Republic World)]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] condemns Macron's "attempts to link Islam with [[terrorism]]" but does not join calls for a boycott of France. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/27/saudi-arabia-condemns-prophets-cartoons-ami-france-turkey-row (Al Jazeera)]
**Protesters burn [[Flag of France|French flag]]s and pictures of Macron outside the French Embassy in [[Baghdad]], [[Iraq]]. [https://www.rudaw.net/english/middleeast/iraq/27102020 (Rudaw)]
**France's [[Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (France)|Foreign Ministry]] warns its citizens to take extra security precautions while traveling in Muslim-majority countries as a Muslim backlash against France grows. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-france-security-boycott/france-warns-citizens-to-be-cautious-as-anger-seethes-in-muslim-world-over-cartoons-idUKKBN27C1IF (Reuters)]
*[[India–United States relations]]
**Following high-level talks in [[Delhi]], [[India]] and the [[United States]] sign a military agreement on sharing sensitive satellite data. The ''Basic Exchange and Cooperation Agreement on Geospatial Cooperation'' (BECA) gives the [[Indian Armed Forces]] access to a range of sensitive geospatial and aeronautical data for military use. Agreements on [[Nuclear power|nuclear energy]], earth sciences and [[alternative medicine]] are also signed. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-54655947 (BBC News)]
*[[Netherlands–Turkey relations]]
**[[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] files a criminal complaint against Dutch [[far-right]] politician and activist [[Geert Wilders]] for allegedly "insulting him on social media". Turkish prosecutors accepted the complaint at an [[Ankara]] court. Erdoğan's lawyers say Wilders insulted "honour, dignity, character and reputation". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-netherlands-erdogan/erdogan-files-criminal-complaint-against-dutch-politician-wilders-idUSKBN27C1PK?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[Killing of Walter Wallace]]
**Protests break out in [[Philadelphia]] after [[Philadelphia Police Department|police]] shoot and kill Walter Wallace, who they say had been armed with a knife. There are also reports of [[vandalism]], including [[looting]], spray painting and smashing of windows at a police station. Police also say 30 officers have been injured, many of which were struck by bricks and other debris, and that 91 protesters were arrested. [https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/local/man-shot-and-killed-by-police-in-west-philadelphia/2574400/ (WCAU-TV)]
*[[2020 Tanzanian general election]]
**Tanzanian political party [[Alliance for Change and Transparency]] (ACT Wazalendo) reports that its [[Zanzibar]] presidential candidate [[Seif Sharif Hamad]] has been arrested following condemnation by him and the political party of the shooting deaths of at least seven civilians amid unrest over alleged fraud on the eve of presidential election. Police confirm Hamad's arrest but do not comment. [https://apnews.com/article/international-news-shootings-tanzania-elections-arrests-9fa98fce198457c50b498e44af86ad1f (AP)]
*[[LGBT rights in Nigeria]]
**A [[Nigeria]]n court throws out a case against 47 men for allegedly publicly engaging in same-sex relationships at a [[Lagos]] hotel in 2018, claiming a lack of diligence on the prosecutor's part. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-lgbt/nigerian-judge-throws-out-case-against-47-men-facing-homosexuality-charge-idUSKBN27C1TZ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**[[Hong Kong independence|Hong Kong pro-independence]] activist [[Tony Chung]] is arrested when he tries to [[seek asylum]] at the U.S. Consulate General. He was on bail for alleged national security law offences. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/oct/27/hong-kong-activist-detained-while-attempting-to-seek-asylum-at-us-consulate (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Australian Aboriginal sacred site]]s
**A [[Eucalyptus melliodora|yellow box tree]] sacred to the women of the [[Djab wurrung]] [[Indigenous Australians|indigenous]] group in western [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] is cut down to make way for a new highway. 50 protesters are arrested at the site for violating [[social distancing]] laws. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2020/oct/27/djab-wurrung-directions-sacred-tree-cut-down-victoria-western-highway-upgrade (''The Guardian'')]
